red-autumn-calville.heading: CALVILLE ROUGE D'AUTOMNE (Autumn Calville; Autumn Red Calville)
red-autumn-calville.flavour: Flesh, white, tinged with red under the skin, and very much so on the side which is exposed to the sun; it is tender, delicate, and juicy, with a pleasant, vinous, and violet scented flavour.
red-autumn-calville.quality: A culinary apple of inferior quality in this country, but highly esteemed on the Continent, both as a culinary and a dessert fruit.
red-autumn-calville.storage: It is in season during October and November.
red-autumn-calville.climate: To have the fruit in perfection it ought to be grown on the paradise stock as an open dwarf, in a fine sandy loam
red-autumn-calville.note: Heading Calville Rouge d'Automne; our aka. Violet-scented.

coccagee.heading: COCCAGEE
coccagee.flavour: Flesh, yellowish white, soft, sharply acid, and austere.
coccagee.quality: One of the oldest and best cider apples
coccagee.storage: in use from October to December.
coccagee.note: 'perhaps the most harsh and austere apple known', yet one of the best for baking, with a rich flavour when cooked.

styre.heading: FOREST STYRE (Stire)
styre.quality: a fine old Gloucestershire cider apple
styre.climate: extensively cultivated on the thin limestone soils of the Forest of Dean
styre.note: Synonym printed as 'Stive' (OCR for Stire). Only 'Flesh, firm'; the cider is 'strong bodied, rich, and highly flavoured'. Hogg also has a separate 'STYRE (Forest Styre)' entry at line 16881 ('One of the oldest Herefordshire cider apples', flesh tender, very juicy) - he lists two apples under the name.

woodcock.heading: WOODCOCK
woodcock.flavour: Flesh, yellowish, sometimes stained with red under the skin, tender, juicy, and acid.
woodcock.note: The old 17th-century Herefordshire cider Woodcock; not Hogg's Sussex culinary Green Woodcock (line 9644).
